newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says it will block East Timor conference.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says it will block East Timor conference.

text.p: Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Thursday the government would block human rights groups from holding a planned conference on East Timor.
But the organisers of the second Asia Pacific Conference on East Timor warned the action would tarnish Malaysia's image as a nation that opposed oppression.
"We cannot say positively now whether we're going ahead with the conference," Sanusi Osman, a spokesman for conference organisers told Reuters. "We'll have to discuss with all the groups involved."
Anwar told reporters the government would seek all legal avenues to prevent the three-day meeting, scheduled for this weekend, from taking place.
"Malaysia should not interfere with Indonesia's domestic problems," Anwar said. "We want to protect our good relationship with Indonesia."
The conference is scheduled for November 9-11 at a Kuala Lumpur hotel. Some 200 people from 24 countries and 75 organisations are expected to gather to denounce Jakarta's rule of East Timor.

Anwar said the government was looking into the proper laws and regulations to use in blocking the conference, adding that the Immigration Department had also been instructed to refuse entry to foreigners attending the meeting.
"This is a decision of the prime minister and Cabinet. If necessary, those who are already here will be asked to leave," Anwar said.
Immigration authorities had earlier refused to allow a Filipino human rights activist into the country for the conference.
Renato Constantino Jr., who organized the first Timor conference in Manila in 1994, was stopped by immigration officials at the Kuala Lumpur airport on Wednesday night, conference organisers said.
Sanusi said the conference had been organised "within the constraints of Malaysian law" and according to guidelines determined by a legal team.

"A heavy-handed crackdown on the conference would tarnish the international gains Malaysia has made to support peaceful resolutions of the troubles in Palestine, South Africa, Cambodia, Bosnia and Mindanao," Sanusi said.
The leader of Malaysia's parliamentary opposition, Lim Kit Siang, deplored Constantino's deportation and the decision to block the conference.

"It is most regrettable that the Malaysian government is not able to make a clear distinction between the views of the government on East Timor and those of Malaysians who want to see a peaceful and negotiated settlement of the 21-year East Timor conflict," he said in a statement.
Indonesia invaded the Portuguese colony of East Timor in December 1975 and annexed it the following year. The United Nations still recognises Lisbon as the administering authority for the territory.
